newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up as RBI mops up dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up as RBI mops up dollar inflows.

text.p: The rupee closed at 35.885/890 against the dollar on Wednesday, up from its 35.92/93 opening, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mopped up large dollar inflows, dealers said.
The rupee saw a high of 35.82 and a low of 35.92 on Wednesday, dealers said. Some dealers said they had heard of stray deals at even 35.94 level in the morning session.
RBI began buying spot dollars in early afternoon, buiying dollars at 35.84/85 level, dealers said.

"After the VSNL news, it was selling all the way," said a dealer, referring to a news item quoting sources close to state-run firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) as saying that it did not plan to bring its GDR funds into India soon.

VSNL raised close to $500 million through its GDR issue earlier this month and the forex market was rife with speculation the money would enter the local market and aggravate the local oversupply of dollars.
Forward dollar premiums opened lower but were steady later.
"Tom spot (tomorrow's spot transactions) was very active today," said a dealer. "Tom spot premiums rose steeply."
"It shows people are squaring up for the year-end," said a dealer, referring to the financial year's close on March 31.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 6.69 percent, down from the previous close of 6.91 percent.
